correctness.rationale: PASS. In a tree any geodesic includes ≤2 pendant edges, and all spine edges lie on the spine-endpoint geodesic, so any edge-general-position set has 0,1 or 2 selected spine edges. With 0, any pendants are compatible; with one e_i, pendants must all be on one side; with two e_i,e_j, selected pendant edges must lie at spine coordinates i+1..j. The converse follows from unique simple paths. Inclusion-maximality forces every allowed pendant, and positivity t_1,t_m≥1 blocks adding other spine edges. The disjoint facet families are P, 2(m−1) left/right ones, and binomial(m−1,2) two-spine ones; count 1+2(m−1)+binomial(m−1,2)=m(m+1)/2, sizes read directly from allowed pendant sums, and minimum formula follows from shortest prefix/suffix/interior block, with m=2 handled separately. Independent fresh BFS shortest-path enumerator checked every subset on 28 test trees with m=2..4 and t_i∈{1,2}, 11,304 edge subsets; computed facets exactly equal structural predictions. Prior packaged verifier reports 60 cases/135,720 subsets, inspected code but not substituted for proof. Does not assert facet result for t_i=0 or arbitrary trees.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. Manuel–Prabha–Klavžar Theorem 3.3 determines only maximum EGP cardinality on trees, whereas the present result counts and sizes all inclusion-maximal sets. Tian–Klavžar–Tan study numerical extremal values and block graphs; a general all-feasible-set polynomial is known and excluded from novelty. Published Resultary spider-tree classification is a different topology (one branching center), not fully whiskered paths with arbitrarily many branching spine vertices.
residual_risks: The standard general-tree cardinality algorithms may be specialized to this caterpillar class, but calculating the all-feasible-set polynomial is not the same as enumerating inclusion-maximal subsets; claim novelty limited to exact facets.
